title: the Glass Steppe Rising Anew
premise: Quentin Underhill has spent his life in the Glass Steppe, a valley where magic cannot follow, serving as the crown's food-taster and quietly building immunity to every poison he sips. When King Aldric declares a realm-wide hunt for the gifted, Quentin is dragged beyond the valley's edge as bait — for his blood carries traces of the old covenant that once bound magic to law. Hunted by the king's witch-finders and courted by fugitive mages who need him to reforge the broken covenant, Quentin must choose between the crown that owns him and the people his survival is being used to destroy. In the end, he renews the covenant at the cost of his own immunity, drinking the valley's poison willingly so magic can return lawfully to both realms.
about_author: Theo Okafor is a former line cook from Lagos who writes fantasy steeped in kitchens, courts, and the quiet violence of service. His work explores what ordinary bodies endure when empires make their choices for them.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Quentin samples a suspect dish at the royal table, detecting bitter almond beneath honeyed quail. Through his POV we learn the rules of his life: never leave the valley, never refuse a plate, never let them see you flinch. The emotional beat is wary pride — he survives by swallowing what would kill anyone else.

chapters.title: A Valley Without Magic
chapters.summary: Quentin walks the Glass Steppe market, where charms fail and hedge-witches are merely eccentric. Flashbacks reveal how his mother fled here pregnant, trading her gift for her child's safety. The beat is longing: a home that protects him by keeping the world out.

chapters.title: The King's Proclamation
chapters.summary: Heralds announce the Gift-Hunt: all bearers of magic must register or die. Quentin watches neighbors denounce each other and feels the valley's sanctuary curdle into complicity. POV shifts briefly to Witch-Finder Serane Voss, who notes the taster's odd bloodwork. The beat is dread arriving on official parchment.

chapters.title: Poisoned Porridge
chapters.summary: Someone poisons the kitchens — not to kill the king, but Quentin specifically, with a compound only magical blood can metabolize. He survives; the cook doesn't. Quentin realizes someone knows what he is. The beat is terror wearing an apron: his safest room becomes a crime scene.

chapters.title: Serane's Questions
chapters.summary: Witch-Finder Voss interrogates Quentin over tea she openly poisoned as a test. He drinks it without dying, sealing his own suspicion. She offers a bargain: serve as living bait to draw fugitive mages, or be declared gifted. The beat is a trap closing politely, cup by cup.

chapters.title: Beyond the Edge
chapters.summary: Escorted past the valley's boundary stones, Quentin feels magic touch him for the first time — a hum in his teeth, colors too bright. His suppressed heritage wakes. The beat is vertigo and grief: the world outside is everything his mother died to keep from him.

chapters.title: The Fugitive Camp
chapters.summary: Voss uses Quentin as bait at a border village; instead of catching mages, he is taken by them. Their leader, the scarred healer Odile, recognizes covenant-blood in him. The beat is disorientation turning to reluctant belonging among people he was sent to betray.

chapters.title: What the Covenant Was
chapters.summary: By firelight, Odile explains the old pact: magic bound itself to law through a mortal vessel's willing oath, renewed each generation. The last vessel broke it and fled into the valley. Quentin's bloodline is the unfinished sentence. The beat is the weight of inheritance he never asked for.

chapters.title: The First Betrayal
chapters.summary: Voss tracks the camp; Quentin must decide whether to warn the mages or let the raid proceed. He burns the witch-finders' supply wagons, choosing sides with arson. The beat is exhilaration shadowed by guilt — he has made himself a criminal to feel honest.

chapters.title: Immunity's Price
chapters.summary: Odile examines Quentin and finds his poison-resistance is killing him slowly: every dose banked in his blood is a debt coming due. To renew the covenant he must survive the Rite of Return, which no half-poisoned body can endure. The beat is mortality made arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Purge Road
chapters.summary: Traveling toward the covenant-stone at the Steppe's heart, the group passes villages where the Hunt has already burned. Quentin witnesses a child mage executed for lighting a candle with a thought. The beat is righteous fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Serane Alone
chapters.summary: In Voss's POV chapters, we learn she hunts the gifted because her sister's uncontrolled gift destroyed their town — justice, to her, is control. She intercepts Quentin's group and offers him clemency one final time. The beat is two wounded people recognizing each other across a drawn blade.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Quentin refuses the pardon publicly, and Voss takes the mages prisoner while letting him flee — a cruelty disguised as mercy. Alone, he confronts the truth that running was always his family's answer. The beat is shame transmuted into decision: he will go back for them.

chapters.title: The King's Table
chapters.summary: Quentin returns to the capital and requests audience as the loyal taster, then poisons the king's wine before the court — nonlethally, proving magic's presence in his blood and forcing Aldric to acknowledge the covenant's terms. The beat is audacity: using his servitude as a weapon.

chapters.title: Trial by Cup
chapters.summary: Aldric, cornered by law he claims to uphold, grants Quentin trial by ordeal: drink the Rite's poison before the assembled realm. If the covenant accepts him, magic returns under law; if not, all mages die and Quentin with them. The beat is a courtroom become altar.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Imprisoned Odile secretly teaches Quentin the rite's true form: the vessel must not resist the poison but welcome it, surrendering the immunity that defined him. He must want to be vulnerable again. The beat is fear of losing the only self he has ever known.

chapters.title: Night Before the Stone
chapters.summary: On the eve of the ordeal, Quentin visits his mother's grave at the valley's edge and finally reads the letter she left him: an apology and a blessing. The beat is quiet reconciliation — forgiveness as preparation.

chapters.title: The Rite of Return
chapters.summary: Before thousands, Quentin drinks the covenant-draught. It tears through his hardened body; visions of every meal he ever survived burn past him. At the edge of death he stops fighting and says yes. The stone accepts him. The beat is transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: Magic Under Law
chapters.summary: The covenant restored, gifts flare lawfully across the realm — registered, bounded, answerable to courts rather than pyres. Voss's witch-finders are dissolved; she watches her sister's memory find peace in the new order. The beat is exhausted relief, justice arriving institutional rather than miraculous.

chapters.title: The Cost Counted
chapters.summary: Quentin recovers fragile and permanently vulnerable — his immunity gone, a simple fever could end him. Odile tends him; the mages he saved now guard him in turn. The beat is tenderness earned: strength redefined as allowing others close.

chapters.title: A New Covenant of Small Things
chapters.summary: Months later, Quentin serves at the king's table still — but now as witness, tasting openly, protected by law he helped write. He trains young vessels and walks the valley freely, magic humming at its borders like a neighbor's music. The beat is homecoming without walls.

chapters.title: The Glass Steppe Rising Anew
chapters.summary: At the valley's spring festival, Quentin raises a cup of ordinary water — the first thing in years he could not survive if it were poisoned — and drinks anyway, among friends. The final beat is chosen vulnerability: survival was never the point; living is.
